claims.text: The initial sub-10 nm equiatomic Au-Co-Cu-Ni-Pt nanoparticles are a single-phase solid solution.
Equiatomic multielement high-entropy alloys can obtain configurational-entropy stabilization of solid solutions.
High-entropy-alloy theory associates lattice distortion and sluggish or hysteretic diffusion with enhanced microstructural and thermal stability.
The sluggish-diffusion mechanism in sub-10 nm Au-Co-Cu-Ni-Pt nanoparticles fails above 600 K.
Above 600 K, surface-energy minimization dominates configurational-entropy stabilization in these nanoparticles.
The surface-to-volume ratio and associated surface-energy contribution increase as particle radius decreases.
For sub-10 nm particles, the surface-energy contribution overrides the bulk configurational-entropy term.
At elevated temperature, the surface-energy driving force represented by 2τ̄/r exceeds barriers associated with lattice distortion, sluggish diffusion, and configurational-entropy stabilization.
The dominance of the surface-energy driving force triggers rapid surface diffusion and atomic exchange.
Au is the lowest-surface-energy element in the Au-Co-Cu-Ni-Pt system.
Rapid atomic transport causes Au to segregate to nanoparticle surfaces.
The smallest particles dissolve and feed larger particles by Ostwald ripening.
Heating will produce a bimodal particle-size distribution.
Particles smaller than 5 nm will disappear and the average particle size will increase.
Heating will produce Au-enriched nanoparticle surfaces.
Anisotropic surface-energy minimization will produce non-spherical particle shapes.
Under the sluggish-diffusion baseline, the particles should retain equiatomic composition and spherical shape up to 1000 K.
The proposed surface-dominated mechanism applies to particles below 10 nm but may not apply to particles above 50 nm or to bulk alloys.
Phase separation can reduce the effective configurational entropy and eliminate behavior attributed to a homogeneous high-entropy solid solution.
Phase stability and decomposition in high-entropy alloys can depend on composition and annealing temperature.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis specifies a breakdown threshold above 600 K, while the uncertainty field states that the exact threshold is unknown without nanoscale diffusion coefficients. The 600 K boundary is therefore presented more definitively than the acknowledged knowledge permits.
